title: Multi-centre validation tests AI-empowered OncoSeek across 15,122 participants and four assay platforms
summary: A 2025 study added four cohorts to evaluate the seven-protein-marker OncoSeek test, which combines blood protein tumor markers and clinical variables with AI. Across seven cohorts from seven centres in China, Brazil and the United States, totaling 15,122 participants, the reported overall sensitivity was 58.4% at 92.0% specificity; the symptomatic cohort had 73.1% sensitivity at 90.6% specificity. The study also tested performance across four platforms and two sample types.
ai_technology: OncoSeek AI-empowered blood test combining seven protein tumor markers with individual clinical data
organization: SeekIn; Henan Cancer Hospital, Peking University Shenzhen Hospital, First Saúde, Yonsei University and collaborating clinical centres

evidence.tested: A 2025 study added four cohorts to evaluate the seven-protein-marker OncoSeek test, which combines blood protein tumor markers and clinical variables with AI.
evidence.unknown: This is a retrospective/observational cohort validation of a blood test, not evidence that screening improves outcomes or reduces mortality. Aggregate sensitivity was 58.4% and performance varied by cancer type; several cancer-specific groups were small. The article adds validation to a previously published OncoSeek test, so this record is limited to the new expanded-cohort/platform result, not a claim of first test discovery.
evidence.ai_role: The AI-assisted test integrated measured protein-marker values and clinical variables for multicancer classification. This paper evaluated its performance in four additional validation cohorts, including a prospective blinded study and symptomatic case-control cohort, and aggregated results across seven cohorts.
